title: After the first failed presentation
opening_case: An analyst forgets a transition during a short update and thinks, “I am terrible at speaking.”

nodes.prompt: An analyst forgets a transition during a short update and thinks, “I am terrible at speaking.” Choose your first response.

choices.text: Ask a colleague for concrete observations
choices.rationale: This preserves a possible evidence-gathering route.

choices.text: Privately replay what happened before seeking feedback
choices.rationale: This is another plausible route; later options may change the result.

nodes.prompt: Colleague says most points were clear. How proceed?

choices.text: Rehearse the transition and try a short follow-up
choices.rationale: Consider practical limits, context and autonomy.

choices.text: Discard the feedback because the mistake proves a label
choices.rationale: Consider whether a broad interpretation exceeds the evidence.

nodes.prompt: A colleague offers no detailed notes. What next?

choices.text: Ask one specific follow-up about the missed transition
choices.rationale: Consider whether an additional observation is possible.

choices.text: Conclude that silence means everyone judged you
choices.rationale: Consider what remains unknown and who else is affected.

nodes.hypothetical_consequence: A specific weakness can become a rehearsal target, while nerves and context still matter.
nodes.tradeoff: This is a possible result, not a prediction. Even careful decisions can produce mixed outcomes because other people, resources and circumstances matter.
nodes.reflection_prompt: Which fact was available, which assumption was made, and what would you revise after new evidence?
